hypothesis.h0: The atom-quark decomposition does not lower wall-clock time to Mission satisfaction against the coarse baseline at a fixed token and tool budget.
hypothesis.h1: The atom-quark decomposition lowers median wall-clock time to Mission satisfaction by at least 15% relative to the coarse baseline at a fixed token and tool budget.

falsification: atom-quark is retained only if its median wall-clock to Mission satisfaction is at least 15% below the coarse baseline over 150 trials per condition (30 workload items x 5 seeds), with the 95% BCa interval on the paired Hodges-Lehmann shift excluding zero. Below 15%, Quark is removed as a first-class concept and Atom decomposition is flattened. If fine beats atom-quark by 15% or more on the same measurement, the global scheduling boundary moves down to the Quark-like primitive.

workloads: 30 repository-level Missions from the Gordian workload corpus
population.sampling: paired on the workload item; the three conditions run in randomized order within each item

effect_size.measure: paired Hodges-Lehmann shift, expressed as a relative reduction versus coarse

analysis_plan.uncertainty: BCa bootstrap 95% CI, 10000 resamples, resampling seed recorded

exclusion_rule: A trial is excluded when the harness crashes before the first dispatch, when the model endpoint returns a transport error on more than 10% of the calls in that trial, or when the workload item's fixture repository fails its own pre-flight test. Excluded trials are retained with their reason and counted in the report. The rule is applied by script before the primary metric is inspected and never by judgement.

environment.source_commit: pinned at run time; the exact commit is recorded in each run.json

threats: planner prompt tuning applied to one decomposition only; controlled by the equal per-arm tuning budget of statistical-contract.md section 3
workload corpus skew toward decomposable Missions
